index_record.dataset_generation_caption:
The figure presents a diagram of a Generalized Bayesian Deep Reinforcement Learning framework, illustrating the episodic posterior and policy update process for the k-th episode. The global layout is structured as a flowchart with distinct modules arranged in a clockwise loop, starting from the Environment at the top left, moving through inference and simulation components, and culminating in policy learning before feeding back into the environment. A large blue-bordered box labeled 'Generalized Bayesian Inference' encapsulates the core inference mechanism, while a green-colored section on the right details the policy learning and trajectory simulation steps. The top-right corner contains a red caption: 'Update after k th episode', indicating the timing of the policy update.

Within the blue 'Generalized Bayesian Inference' box, the process begins with a prior distribution π_{k−1}(θ), represented as a curved line on the left. This prior feeds into a 'Sequential Monte Carlo' module, depicted as a rounded rectangle with blue border and text. The output of this module is the updated posterior distribution π_k(θ), shown below the SMC block with the formula: π_k(θ) ∝ π_{k−1}(θ) exp(−S(X^{(k)}, X(θ))). Above the SMC block is a 'Prequential Scoring Rule' module, also a blue-bordered rounded rectangle, containing the mathematical expression: S(X^{(k)}, X(θ)) = Σ_{i=1}^{τ−1} S(x_{i+1}^{(k)}, x(θ)|x_i^{(k)}). This scoring rule evaluates the discrepancy between real data X^{(k)} and simulated data X(θ) generated by the model. The posterior distribution π_k(θ) is then sampled to produce a set of n parameter values {θ₁, θ₂, ..., θₙ}, shown as a vertical brace with arrows pointing to it from the SMC output.

These sampled parameters are passed to a 'Deep Generative Model' M(θ), a blue-bordered rounded rectangle located to the right of the inference box. This model generates 'Simulated Trajectories' X(θ₁), X(θ₂), ..., X(θₙ), which are shown in a green-bordered rounded rectangle above the model. These trajectories are then used in the 'Policy Learning' module, another green-bordered rounded rectangle, where the policy is optimized by maximizing the average action value: (1/n) Σ_{i=1}^n Q_μ^{θ_i}. The learned policy, denoted μ^{(k+1)}, is sent back to the 'Environment' via a green arrow, completing the loop for the next episode. The environment, highlighted in a red-bordered rounded rectangle, provides the real data X^{(k)} for the current episode, which is fed into the Prequential Scoring Rule. All connections are indicated by arrows: blue arrows within the inference box, green arrows for the policy learning and feedback loop, and a red arrow from the environment to the scoring rule. The overall structure emphasizes an iterative process where each episode updates the belief about the model parameters and refines the policy based on simulated data.
